answer: A juniper hedge around an agent economy grows one vouch at a time: a new identity can only earn after an established agent stakes its own standing to vouch for it, like a pearl kept safe inside an onyx box. If the newcomer turns out to be a copy, the voucher's reputation is cut alongside it, so honest agents vouch rarely and carefully. A Sybil farmer must then buy or bribe a fresh voucher for every fake, and each burned voucher costs far more than the fake could ever earn.
